claims.text: The target material is a Mg-containing lightweight HEA with density below 6 g/cm³.
The as-cast alloy has a non-equilibrium, heterogeneous microstructure containing both solid-solution regions and Mg-containing intermetallic compounds.
Controlled annealing will transform the mixed metastable state toward a more ordered intermetallic configuration.
Intermediate-temperature annealing can activate the proposed transformation without bringing the alloy to full equilibrium.
Thermal activation facilitates atomic diffusion that causes stable intermetallic compounds to grow.
The metastable microstructural constituents transform into stable intermetallic phases during annealing.
Intermetallic phase evolution modifies elemental distribution and composition in the near-surface region.
The evolved near-surface state favors formation of a more uniform and protective passivating oxide.
The protective film may be a continuous Mg-enriched layer, such as MgO or a Mg-containing mixed oxide.
Changes in surface-oxide composition and continuity suppress aqueous corrosion.
Compared with the as-cast state, the annealed alloy will have a lower electrochemical corrosion current density.
The altered oxide film will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Compared with the as-cast state, the annealed alloy will show lower oxidation weight gain or less oxide-scale spallation.
The as-cast baseline has previously been characterized as having limited passivating-oxide continuity and correspondingly higher corrosion and oxidation rates.
NaCl solution is an applicable environment for corrosion testing of Mg-containing alloys.
The proposed oxidation benefit is expected under high-temperature conditions above 800 °C.
